summary: Boise NF Gold Fork lookout (Valley County): a 1918-20 rock-ledge platform, a 1933 L-4 cabin moved in 1988 to the Crawford Work Center near Cascade; sources disagree on elevation.

facts.design: R1/L-4 cabin on a concrete base (1933), replacing an open platform on a rock ledge (c. 1918-20)
facts.status_note: Original platform site listed as gone; the 1933 cabin moved in 1988 to the Crawford Forest Work Center northeast of Cascade. The latest visual record in the sources is a 2012 register photo caption.

staffing.status: Mr. and Mrs. Wayne Barney (1935 newspaper item); Edna Cantwell (1945 newspaper item); Milton Greenlee as lookout in August 1955 photo captions; no full staff list in the sources read

access.note: Relocated cabin sits at the Forest Service's Crawford Work Center. Idaho Fire Lookouts marks it drive-up, but no source says whether the public may visit.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest

events.note: Open platform on a rock ledge reached by a long staircase; NHLR says the site began operation circa 1918-20, Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1918-1920; firelookout.com says a 6x6 log platform was established in the late 1910s
R1/L-4 cabin on a 10-foot 20x20 concrete base, built two miles from the original location (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts); firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts also give 1933
Mr. and Mrs. Wayne Barney spent the summer at the station, per a Payette Valley Sentinel item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Edna Cantwell of Boise served at the lookout, working out of Cascade, per an Idaho Statesman item quoted by Forest Lookouts
August 1955 National Archives photos by Bluford W. Muir; captions name Mr. Milton Greenlee as lookout and Ranger LeRoy Sprague

Cabin moved to the Crawford Forest Work Center northeast of Cascade (NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts); firelookout.com says two miles east of Cascade for private use; Forest Lookouts says the Crawford Ranger Station
NHLR photo caption: cabin relocated to the Crawford Forest Work Center, Cascade, Idaho (courtesy Ron Kemnow)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the 2012 register photo caption place the cabin at the Crawford Forest Work Center northeast of Cascade. Firelookout.com says two miles east of Cascade for private use, and Forest Lookouts says the Crawford Ranger Station. This record follows the register and its 2012 photo.
NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe an open platform on a rock ledge; firelookout.com describes a 6x6 log platform atop a rock. Both descriptions are recorded; no source settles it.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict left open: 4,889 ft (1,490 m) on NHLR vs 7,790 ft on firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. The brief's location conflict is unresolved: firelookout.org list coordinates 44.67137, -115.83580 (matches brief ffla) vs 44.65839, -115.83738 (Idaho list, per brief). Story uses no coordinates. The record us-id-gold-fork-at-crawford-work-center covers the same cabin; this record leads with the original site. Idaho Fire Lookouts carries National Archives photos from August 1955 (Greenlee, Sprague, Muir) but no image URLs were captured, so no photo entries were added. The 1955 staffing comes from photo captions, not a staff list.
